requirements.requirement: The system shall prevent creation of schedules that assign a student to two places at the same time.
requirements.source_citation: it should stop me from scheduling a student in two places at the same time
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly requests prevention of double-booking; this is a quality requirement about correctness/validation rather than a new functional feature. Missing specifics: whether this check applies across all schedule types, time zones, recurring events, or tentative bookings; no error message/override policy specified.
requirements.follow_up_question: Should the system block creation of any overlapping assignments automatically (hard stop), or allow an override with justification in certain roles? If overrides are allowed, which roles can override and should the override be audited?

requirements.requirement: The system shall warn or block assignments when an instructor or other resource is already booked for the same time period.
requirements.source_citation: or assign an instructor who is already booked
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder wants conflict detection for instructors; indicates need for validation on resource availability. Gaps: what constitutes 'booked' (confirmed vs tentative), minimum granularity (minutes), and whether to block or warn.
requirements.follow_up_question: How should the system treat tentative vs confirmed bookings, and what time granularity (e.g., minutes) should conflict checks use?

requirements.requirement: The system shall check required clearances for a student and warn or block assignment to placements that require clearances the student does not have.
requirements.source_citation: It could warn me if a clinical placement requires a clearance the student doesn't have
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly requests validation against clearance requirements; this concerns compliance and safety. Unclear whether some clearances are mandatory (block) vs advisory (warn), and which clearance types and authoritative sources will be used.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which specific clearance types should be treated as blocking versus warning, and where will the authoritative clearance data come from (university system or manual entry)?

requirements.requirement: The system shall send automatic notifications to students, instructors, and site contacts immediately when a schedule change occurs.
requirements.source_citation: When a schedule changes, students, instructors, and the site people should get told right away.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requests immediate notifications to stakeholders to avoid missed updates. Gaps: definition of 'immediately' (seconds?), permitted channels, batching behavior, opt-outs, and delivery guarantees.
requirements.follow_up_question: What maximum delay counts as 'immediate' for notifications (e.g., within 30 seconds), and which channels (email, SMS, push) are mandatory for each user role?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide delivery and acknowledgement tracking for notifications and report which recipients have not confirmed receipt.
requirements.source_citation: some way to know they saw it — or at least that it was sent. It would be nice if the system could tell me who hasn't confirmed
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder needs traceability of notifications and the ability to follow up with non-confirming recipients. Gaps: what constitutes 'confirmation' (read receipt, click, explicit acknowledge), retention of these logs, and privacy concerns.
requirements.follow_up_question: How should users confirm notifications (read receipt, acks via link/button, or reply), and how long must confirmation records be retained?

requirements.requirement: The system shall display UI responses for simple actions (e.g., retrieving a student record or changing a shift) within 5 seconds under normal conditions.
requirements.source_citation: For little things like pulling up a student's record or changing a shift, I hate waiting — it should be almost instant... if it takes longer than, say, five seconds, I start clicking again
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder gave explicit acceptable latency for routine UI actions: under ~5 seconds. Gaps: definition of 'normal conditions', percentile target (e.g., 95th percentile), and whether this applies to all user roles and network conditions.
requirements.follow_up_question: Should the 5-second target apply to the 95th percentile of requests during business hours, and does it apply to both local and remote users?

requirements.requirement: The system shall complete batch schedule generation operations within 30 seconds under expected load.
requirements.source_citation: For the whole schedule generator... half a minute-ish feels like the outside of acceptable
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder specified acceptable upper bound for batch job latency (~30s). Missing specifics: batch size, concurrency, whether background processing with progress indicators is acceptable, and performance SLAs.
requirements.follow_up_question: What are typical sizes for a 'full schedule generation' (number of students/shifts), and should longer runs be allowed as background jobs with progress and notifications?

requirements.requirement: The system shall support simultaneous use by at least 15 concurrent users without performance degradation.
requirements.source_citation: Maybe around ten people? Ten to fifteen on busy days, I guess. So it has to handle that load without choking.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder described expected peak concurrency (10–15) and expectation of acceptable performance under that load. Gaps: peak distribution, burstiness, and future growth expectations.
requirements.follow_up_question: Is there an expected growth in concurrent users over the next 2–3 years we should design for, or is 15 a stable long-term peak?

requirements.requirement: The system shall be available during business hours with an initial target availability of at least 95%.
requirements.source_citation: I wouldn't want it down more than a few percent of the time. If I had to pick a number, something like ninety-five percent availability sounds about right to me for the start.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder quantified acceptable availability (≈95%) and emphasized business-hour availability. Gaps: definition of business hours, measurement window (monthly), maintenance windows, and higher targets for mature service.
requirements.follow_up_question: Please confirm the definition of 'business hours' (days/times) and whether availability should be measured monthly or annually for SLA purposes.

requirements.requirement: The system shall support role-based access control so that program admins have full access while site coordinators and instructors see only the student and placement details necessary for their role.
requirements.source_citation: program admins — the core staff — need a full view... Site coordinators shouldn't see the full student files; they only need details relevant to the placement... Instructors probably need rosters and schedule info, but not private notes.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly requests RBAC with differentiated views. Gaps: exact role definitions, permission matrix, delegation and admin capabilities, and how role changes are managed.
requirements.follow_up_question: Can you provide a list of user roles and the specific data elements each role must be able to view or modify?

requirements.requirement: The system shall enforce university privacy and information policies, restricting access to student health and background-check information to authorized staff only.
requirements.source_citation: student health or background-check info should be tightly controlled. We have university policies about privacy, and the system should follow those
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requires compliance with university policies for sensitive data. Gaps: the exact policies, regulatory requirements (FERPA, HIPAA), encryption/storing requirements, and audit obligations.
requirements.follow_up_question: Can the compliance office provide the university policies (e.g., FERPA/HIPAA mapping) so we can specify required controls (encryption, access logs, retention)?

requirements.requirement: The system shall maintain an audit trail recording who changed data, what was changed, and when, and make these logs available for reporting and compliance review.
requirements.source_citation: audit trails would be great — knowing who changed what and when
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly requests audit trails for accountability and compliance. Gaps: retention duration, immutability, scope of audit (notifications, views, config), and access controls to audit logs.
requirements.follow_up_question: What is the required audit log retention period and which events must be captured (create/read/update/delete, notification sends/acks, permission changes)?

requirements.requirement: The system shall integrate with the university student records system (SIS) and HR/payroll to avoid duplicate data entry, with integrations planned from project start and phased as necessary.
requirements.source_citation: It should tie into the university's student records for enrollments and probably our HR or payroll for instructor assignments, so we don't have to enter data twice.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requires interoperability with SIS and HR systems to prevent duplicate data. Gaps: integration protocols (API/flat files), mandatory vs phased on-day-one requirement, and data synchronization frequency/conflict resolution.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which university systems (product names or APIs) should we integrate with and are there preferred integration methods (real-time API, nightly batch CSV import)?

requirements.requirement: The system shall be planned to allow phased integration rollout, but manual imports should be supported as a temporary workaround.
requirements.source_citation: It should be planned from the start, but if we have to phase it, that's okay as long as the roadmap includes it. Manual imports are a pain, though, so sooner is better.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder accepts phased delivery but prefers earlier integration; manual imports acceptable short-term. Gaps: acceptable manual import formats, frequency, and responsibility for mapping/validation.
requirements.follow_up_question: What manual import formats (CSV templates) would you accept during phased rollout, and who will be responsible for performing imports?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide clear warnings for non-critical validation issues and block saving for critical conflicts such as overlapping times, with the ability to acknowledge warnings where appropriate.
requirements.source_citation: For some things it should block saving until fixed — overlapping times, for instance. For other things, like missing a non-critical clearance, a clear warning that you can acknowledge might be okay.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder distinguishes between hard constraints and overridable warnings; expects clear user affordances. Gaps: list of critical vs non-critical checks, who can acknowledge, and if acknowledgements are audited.
requirements.follow_up_question: Can you provide a prioritized list of validations that must be blocking versus warnings, and which roles may acknowledge warnings?

requirements.requirement: The system shall be usable in standard web browsers without requiring special plugins or proprietary installations.
requirements.source_citation: If a system needs special plugins or only works in one browser, it becomes a training and support nightmare... We need something that just opens in whatever regular browser people have
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requires cross-browser compatibility and avoidance of plugins to reduce support overhead. Gaps: supported browser versions, offline behavior, and accessibility standards.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which browsers and minimum versions must be supported, and are there accessibility standards (WCAG) we must meet?

requirements.requirement: The system shall be usable on tablets for quick checks and shall support phones for receiving alerts but may limit full scheduling functionality to larger screens.
requirements.source_citation: It should at least be usable on a tablet for quick checks. Phones are useful for receiving alerts but not for heavy lifting like building schedules.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requests responsive design with read/alert support on phones and tablet usability for light tasks. Gaps: which exact features must be available on tablet vs phone and responsive breakpoints.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which specific functions must be available on tablet and which (if any) on phone (e.g., view rosters, acknowledge notifications)?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide basic reporting capabilities including daily clinical rosters per site, instructor assignments, and summaries of students missing required clearances.
requirements.source_citation: daily clinical rosters for sites, instructor assignments, and a summary of who is missing required clearances
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder enumerated specific report types desired to save time over spreadsheet work. Gaps: report formats (PDF/CSV), scheduling/automation of reports, and performance expectations for report generation.
requirements.follow_up_question: What output formats do you need for reports (CSV/PDF), and should reports be schedulable/emailed automatically?

requirements.requirement: The system shall reduce dependence on printed artifacts by providing on-screen rosters and sharing features to replace routine printing workflows.
requirements.source_citation: It'd be nice if the system reduced the amount we have to print. Less paper, fewer trips to the printer
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder desires digital workflows to cut printing; implies requirements for display, export, and sharing. Gaps: which printed artifacts are critical to replace and if printed copies will still be required by any external sites.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which specific printed artifacts do you want eliminated first, and do any clinical sites require printed rosters as a compliance requirement?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide rescheduling workflows that check for conflicts, update rosters, and send notifications to all affected parties automatically.
requirements.source_citation: I click a student or a shift, choose a new slot or site, and the system checks conflicts, sends notifications to everyone affected, and updates the roster
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder expects automation in rescheduling to reduce manual emailing; it's a usability/operational quality requirement about end-to-end behavior. Gaps: transactional guarantees (atomicity of change + notifications), rollback behavior, and concurrency handling.
requirements.follow_up_question: Should rescheduling changes and notifications be transactional (either all succeed or none), and how should conflicts detected during rescheduling be surfaced to the user?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide reporting or UI indicators showing cohort progression and students who are behind or need intervention.
requirements.source_citation: a snapshot of cohort progression, so I can see who's on track and who needs intervention
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder needs analytics to identify at-risk students; this affects usability and reporting. Gaps: metrics defining 'on track', data sources, update frequency, and visualization preferences.
requirements.follow_up_question: What specific metrics define 'on track' for cohort progression and how frequently must those metrics be updated?

requirements.requirement: The system shall expose who has not confirmed notifications and provide tools to follow up (e.g., resend or escalate).
requirements.source_citation: It would be nice if the system could tell me who hasn't confirmed, so I can follow up.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requires operational visibility into notification acknowledgements and the ability to act on non-responses. Gaps: escalation rules, automated retries, and permission to trigger follow-ups.
requirements.follow_up_question: Should follow-up actions be manual only, or should the system support automated retries and escalation workflows after configurable timeouts?

requirements.requirement: The system shall enforce university data retention and access policies, including retention durations and access restrictions provided by the university compliance office.
requirements.source_citation: The university also has rules about how long we keep data and who can access it, so the system should respect those rules.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder indicates need to comply with institutional retention/access policies. Gaps: exact retention periods, archival/secure deletion mechanisms, and legal hold handling.
requirements.follow_up_question: Can the compliance office provide required retention schedules and any legal-hold procedures we must implement?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide clear, intuitive UI workflows so that core staff can be productive after one day of focused training and adjuncts/site coordinators after a shorter orientation.
requirements.source_citation: maybe one day of training should be enough for most folks to be productive... adjuncts and site coordinators should be able to use it for the bits they need, but they won't want a long session
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder sets a learnability target (1 day for core staff, shorter for others). Gaps: success metrics for training effectiveness, documentation needs, and support channels during rollout.
requirements.follow_up_question: What key workflows must be covered in the one-day training, and how will we measure training success (e.g., task completion time, number of support tickets)?

requirements.requirement: The system shall handle typical staff hardware diversity and older machines by working in standard browsers without requiring high-end client hardware.
requirements.source_citation: Some of our staff are on Mac, some on Windows, some use older machines. If a system needs special plugins or only works in one browser, it becomes a training and support nightmare.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder wants client-agnostic solution that minimizes support; implies constraints on resource usage and client-side processing. Gaps: minimum device specs and network bandwidth expectations.
requirements.follow_up_question: What is the minimum acceptable client hardware and network bandwidth we should design for (e.g., 4+ year-old machines, 3G mobile)?

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide mechanisms to reduce manual spreadsheet work by automating common reports and exports to standard formats.
requirements.source_citation: It doesn't have to be fancy, but it should save me time compared to cobbling things together in a spreadsheet.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder expects efficiency gains over current spreadsheet-based processes through automation and exports. Gaps: exact export formats needed and degree of automation desired (scheduled exports, APIs).
requirements.follow_up_question: Which spreadsheet exports or automated exports are highest priority, and do you need API access for downstream analytics?

requirements.requirement: The system shall track and report system outages and provide advance notice of scheduled maintenance impacting business hours.
requirements.source_citation: it should be up pretty much all the time during our working hours... allow for rare outages
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder expects high availability and transparency about outages; requires operational notification capability. Gaps: notification channels for outages, acceptable maintenance windows, and SLA reporting frequency.
requirements.follow_up_question: What notification channels and lead times are required for scheduled maintenance, and how should outage metrics be reported to your team?
